comment: The cross-language conformance table for path classification.
Read by the TypeScript guard's tests (src/adapters/allowlist.test.ts) and by the Rust
transport's tests (src-tauri/src/exchange_guard.rs). Both implementations must agree on
every row, so neither can drift without a test failing on one side or the other.
The awkward cases are the point: /sapi/v1/capital/withdraw/history reads withdrawals and
must be allowed, /sapi/v1/capital/withdraw/apply performs one and must not be, and the
difference between them is entirely in the last segment.

Punctuation-disguised entries were added after adversarial testing: the path grammar permits '.', '_' and '-', so whole-segment matching let 'order.' and 'order.json' through. Both classifiers tokenise on that punctuation.
wildcardComment: A trailing wildcard is the hole an allowlist alone cannot close: '/api/v3/*' admits
'/api/v3/order' while looking innocent in review. So the concrete path of every outbound
request is classified again at send time, not only when the list was written.
